purpose: Guard AI Client registry, enum, cache, and kill-switch calls with capability probes so older WP 7.0 / older-SDK installs fail open instead of fataling.
riskRationale: Additive guards with fail-open fallbacks only; no setting keys, option I/O, or registration flow changed. Residual risk is limited to untested fallback branches and two remaining unguarded throw paths.

text: Net-positive compat hardening that matches its stated intent and preserves hard rules (separate settings, credential-blind bust hooks). Well-scoped probes with sensible version fallbacks. Remaining gaps are small: one unguarded throw path in cache busting, one unsafe cast in the exception-message path, silent early returns, and no tests for the new fallback branches.

reasoning: PR is close but two leftover fatal paths (getCache throw, exception-message cast) directly undercut its no-fatal claim and are trivial to fix; plus no coverage for the new branches.

message: method_exists probe on AiClient::defaultRegistry plus is_object/method_exists on the registry instance is the right fail-open pattern — older SDKs return early instead of fataling with undefined-method Error.
VERSION reads via defined() with oldest-shape fallbacks avoid undefined-constant fatals while preserving the 5/6/7-arg ProviderMetadata version gating.
Kill-switch check correctly probes defaultRegistry and isProviderConfigured with nested try/catch per provider, preserving the non-blocking render behavior.
Cache guards (class_exists+method_exists on getCache, is_object+method_exists on delete) plus transient fallback keep bust hooks credential-blind per wp.org review rule.

AiClient::getCache() is probed for existence but not wrapped in try/catch. If the SDK method exists yet throws (corrupted cache, older-SDK signature mismatch), the exception bubbles out of bustCaches/bustCachesAdd, which run on update_option/add_option hooks and could break settings saves.
suggestion: Wrap the getCache() call in try/catch and fall back to null (transient-only bust) so cache busting never breaks option updates.

message: Exception-message builder calls method_exists($capability, 'getValue') without an is_object guard and falls back to (string)$capability. For a non-stringable object without getValue this throws an Error (not the documented RuntimeException); for a non-object/non-string scalar it can TypeError on method_exists. This is the exact legacy-shape path the PR claims to harden.
suggestion: Guard with is_object before method_exists and fall back to get_class()/get_debug_type() instead of a blind string cast.

message: Both new early returns (missing defaultRegistry, malformed registry) are silent, unlike the existing catch blocks that error_log under WP_DEBUG. On an older SDK the providers will just be absent with no diagnostic trail.
suggestion: Add WP_DEBUG-gated error_log lines matching the existing pattern before each early return.

message: No test coverage for any new fallback branch (missing getSupportedCapabilities, legacy getValue/string capabilities, missing enum factories, VERSION fallbacks). The PR description claims 6 tests pass but none exercise the guarded paths, so the core no-fatal claim is unverified.
suggestion: Add Brain Monkey / PHPUnit unit tests with stub legacy ModelMetadata and missing-enum scenarios asserting fail-open behavior (RuntimeException, not Error) and fallback version strings.
